dedupe_keys.name: uc berkeley disaster evacuation surveys 2017 hurricane irma 2017 southern california wildfires and 2018 carr wildfire

description: These three surveys record how people decided whether and how to evacuate in three disasters in the United States: Hurricane Irma in Florida in 2017, the December 2017 Southern California wildfires and the 2018 Carr Wildfire around Redding, California. The producers are Stephen Wong, Joan Walker and Susan Shaheen at the University of California, Berkeley, who distributed the online surveys through local partners; for the Carr Fire these were transport and emergency management agencies, local governments, community organisations and news outlets. Coverage: 1,263 valid responses for Irma, 552 for the Southern California fires and 647 for the Carr Fire, of which 645, 226 and 284 cleaned responses were used for choice modelling. Each survey asks about risk perception, communications, evacuation decisions, potential use of the sharing economy in disasters (such as shared rides or housing), opinions of evacuation management, and demographics. The data are available as free CSV files with the questionnaires on Zenodo under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: respondents were self-selected through online channels with a prize draw, so samples are not representative, many responses are incomplete, and home locations are coarse. Simulation uses: estimating evacuation decision and departure time models, calibrating agent-based evacuation simulations for wildfires and hurricanes, and testing warning strategies. Related records: the evacuation route choice web experiment (data-evacuation-route-choice-web-experiment) and PyroRL (model-pyrorl) cover evacuation choices and decisions.
